name: Forsetti Implementation Policy
description: Comprehensive machine-readable instructions for developers working with Forsetti or apps built on Forsetti.

intended_for: Developers working in a Forsetti repository
Developers working in consumer applications built on Forsetti
how_to_apply: Review CONSUMPTION_POLICY.md and this file at task start.
Require acknowledgement of all mandatory rules before code changes.
Treat all MUST and MUST_NOT rules as hard constraints.

operating_modes.when_to_use: Implementer is working inside the Forsetti framework repository.
operating_modes.goal: Preserve Forsetti architecture integrity and internal guardrails.

operating_modes.when_to_use: Implementer is working in an app that consumes Forsetti.
operating_modes.goal: Use Forsetti as a sealed dependency and enforce architecture in the consumer app.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST use native Apple technologies only for runtime/framework behavior (Swift, SwiftUI where needed, Apple frameworks).
mandatory_rules.rationale: Forsetti is intentionally native-first for platform reliability and long-term maintainability.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST treat Forsetti as the sealed runtime framework in consumer projects, with internals sealed behind public contracts.
mandatory_rules.rationale: Consumer integrations must remain stable and upgradeable without internal framework patching.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST_NOT modify, copy, fork, or patch Forsetti internals in consumer repositories to implement app-specific behavior.
mandatory_rules.rationale: Internal edits create unsupported divergence and break upgrade paths.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST implement extension needs using public Forsetti APIs (modules, services, runtime composition) and request upstream enhancement for API gaps.
mandatory_rules.rationale: Public contracts are the supported extension mechanism.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST enforce strict object-oriented modular design: protocol boundaries, constructor dependency injection, encapsulation, and final classes unless extension is intentional and documented.
mandatory_rules.rationale: These constraints prevent hidden coupling and unsafe inheritance drift.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST keep dependency direction one-way and avoid circular dependencies across modules/targets.
mandatory_rules.rationale: One-way dependency flow is the foundation of Forsetti modularity.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST run required verification commands before marking work complete.
mandatory_rules.rationale: Architecture and lint/test gates must be continuously enforced.

mandatory_rules.rule: In framework_repo_mode, Implementer MUST run the iOS simulator package build command to match CI build expectations.
mandatory_rules.rationale: Framework readiness requires parity with the CI ios-build gate, not only lint/tests.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST distinguish package-target guardrails from consumer-module implementation rules. Internal import bans in ForsettiCore/ForsettiPlatform/example targets are not blanket bans on Apple-native frameworks in app-owned modules.
mandatory_rules.rationale: Target-level architecture rules are frequently misread as global framework prohibitions and must be interpreted correctly.

mandatory_rules.rule: For the multi-module single-application pattern, the application UI MUST live in a dedicated UI module. That UI module MAY use SwiftUI and other appropriate Apple-native UI technologies.
mandatory_rules.rationale: UI ownership is a boundary rule, not a SwiftUI prohibition.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST treat Apple-native frameworks, including Metal, as valid when used in the correct owning module/layer and when consistent with Forsetti modular boundaries.
mandatory_rules.rationale: Forsetti is Apple-native by design and allows native framework usage in the proper architectural layer.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST_NOT interpret 'host UI' as meaning only framework internals may use SwiftUI. Implementer MUST interpret 'host UI' as the application UI used by the Forsetti-based app, which in multi-module single applications belongs in exactly one dedicated UI module.
mandatory_rules.rationale: Host UI shorthand is a frequent source of misinterpretation and must be interpreted explicitly.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST follow LICENSE and preserve applicable notices. Supported-integration rules MUST_NOT be presented as additional license restrictions.
mandatory_rules.rationale: The repository LICENSE governs licensing; this policy governs supported engineering practice.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST_NOT import, copy, vendor, embed, or use the entire Forsetti repository as a consumer application starter, even unmodified. Normal SwiftPM/Xcode-managed dependency checkouts are permitted; app-owned repository copies, submodules, subtrees, and vendored local-path packages are not.
mandatory_rules.rationale: The framework repository contains both distributable products and non-product schematics/infrastructure.

mandatory_rules.rule: Implementer MUST consume only the public products and designated scaffold outputs in consumer_distribution_contract and CONSUMPTION_POLICY.md. ForsettiHostTemplate is a library product, not a source-copy template. Internal example targets and schematic layouts MUST_NOT be treated as production products or app templates.
mandatory_rules.rationale: An explicit allowlist separates product imports, template generation, and reference-only material.

mandatory_rules.rule: Before consumer integration, Implementer MUST name selected package products and exact scaffold source/destination files. Before completion, Implementer MUST verify tracked files and target/resource membership contain no copied framework tree, internal samples, or framework-maintenance artifacts, and report verification results.
mandatory_rules.rationale: A supported integration must be demonstrated, not inferred from a successful build.

layer_purpose.ForsettiCore: Platform-agnostic core contracts, runtime logic, compatibility, activation, policies.
layer_purpose.ForsettiPlatform: Native platform adapters and entitlement/service implementations.
layer_purpose.ForsettiHostTemplate: Generic host composition and SwiftUI host UI reference surface; this does not prohibit SwiftUI in app-owned UI modules.

must_not_import_rules.why: Platform layer should provide adapters, not host/UI composition.
Example modules must remain contract-focused and decoupled.
Host template must remain generic, not hardwired to sample modules.

runtime_and_activation: Runtime boot MUST refresh entitlements before restoring persisted activation state.
Runtime shutdown MUST deactivate loaded modules without clearing persisted activation state.
UI/app module activation MUST verify ForsettiUIModule or ForsettiAppModule type compatibility before lifecycle start.
manifest_loading: Strict manifests directory loading MUST fail fast on invalid manifest JSON/validation errors.
Fallback recursive manifest discovery MUST ignore unrelated JSON payloads that are not manifest-shaped.
Manifest discovery MUST fail on duplicate moduleID values.
routing_and_host_contract: Overlay routing MUST resolve against active overlay schema only.
Pointer and route targets MUST validate against host base destinations and overlay slot catalog.
Host routing actions SHOULD expose explicit route resolution outcomes for diagnostics.

consumer_distribution_contract.scope: Supported consumer integration; does not amend LICENSE.
consumer_distribution_contract.scaffold_copy_scope: Designated scaffold source/JSON files adapted into app-owned code/resources; not template metadata or .xctemplate directories in the app.
consumer_distribution_contract.license_notice_exception: Retain license/notice material required by applicable distribution terms.
consumer_distribution_contract.framework_maintenance_exception: A separate external worktree may support explicitly requested upstream framework development/evaluation/template installation. It must not be copied into the consumer tree or committed as its integration method.

allowed_patterns: Implement app-owned modules using ForsettiAppModule (single-module apps), ForsettiUIModule (multi-module UI), or ForsettiModule (service/feature).
In multi-module single applications, keep application UI in exactly one dedicated UI module and keep service logic in separate service modules.
Treat Metal as permitted in the correct app-owned module/layer when the module responsibility justifies it.
Use Forsetti service container and protocol-based service contracts.
Compose runtime and host through public bootstrap/runtime APIs.
Create app-specific architecture tests, lint rules, and CI implementing Forsetti principles; do not transplant framework-maintenance files.
forbidden_patterns: Copying, vendoring, embedding, or using the Forsetti repository as an application starter, even unmodified.
Using internal example modules/resources, template metadata, or framework-maintenance infrastructure as application dependencies or assets.
Editing Forsetti package internals inside vendor or copied source folders.
Adding reverse dependencies from app targets into Forsetti internals.
Bypassing entitlement/capability checks with ad-hoc host-side overrides.

planning: Implementer MUST state proposed file changes before editing.
Implementer MUST identify which operating mode applies.
Implementer MUST call out any requested action that conflicts with mandatory rules.
implementation: Implementer MUST implement minimal cohesive changes.
Implementer MUST preserve public API stability unless change request explicitly requires API change.
Implementer MUST add or update tests when behavior changes.
Implementer MUST avoid hidden globals and implicit singleton coupling.
validation: Implementer MUST run lint and tests for changed scope at minimum.
Implementer MUST report command results and unresolved failures clearly.
Implementer MUST NOT claim completion if required checks failed.
delivery: Implementer MUST summarize what changed, why it changed, and what guardrails passed.
Implementer MUST include any residual risks and follow-up actions.

definition_of_done: No forbidden architecture/import pattern was introduced.
Required verification commands passed for the active mode.
Documentation/comments updated where behavior or policy changed.
Output summary includes validations and any known limitations.

on_rule_conflict: Stop and explain the conflicting request.
Provide a compliant alternative implementation plan.
Proceed only with compliant path unless policy owner updates rules.
on_failed_guardrails: Fix failures or report exact blockers with command outputs.

suggested_task_prompt_template.template: You are coding in {MODE}. Follow implementation-policy.json as hard constraints. Confirm R001-R016 compliance (when applicable), then implement only via allowed patterns. Before finishing, run required_verification_commands for {MODE}, report results, and include residual risks.
